intro: Driver/sales workers combine driving, customer service and route planning, skills that delivery, postal and freight jobs reward. The closest of the 25 careers below is Couriers and Messengers, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $39,200, about 1% more than the $38,770 driver/sales workers earn.
why_it_works: A route day means loading the truck, meeting store or home customers, taking orders and handling payments on a schedule. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for this job, and time management and problem solving at 3. Postal, freight and shipping jobs use the same mix. All matches need no extra schooling. To earn more, build skills in instructing and analyzing operations.
tips: The Postal Service is the best-paid close option: mail carriers earn $60,550, which is 56% more.
Cargo and Freight Agents earn $52,260, or 35% more, if you prefer arranging shipments to driving.
Keep your driving record clean and note your sales results; both count in every match.

faq.q: What jobs can former driver/sales workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Couriers and Messengers (89%), Parking Attendants (83%) and Postal Service Mail Carriers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Shipping, receiving and inventory clerks are also 82% matched and earn $45,260, which is 17% more than the $38,770 driver/sales median.

faq.q: Which careers for driver/sales workers pay more?
faq.a: 13 of the 25 matches pay more. Postal Service Clerks earn $62,130 (60% more), mail carriers $60,550 (56% more) and Cargo and Freight Agents $52,260 (35% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Postal jobs require passing an entrance process.

faq.q: Do driver/sales workers need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than driver/sales workers already have, including all of the top 10. In a close match, 61% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and training often takes a month or less.

faq.q: What skills should driver/sales workers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, operations analysis, equipment selection and programming. Social perceptiveness already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so training others or planning routes and logistics is the usual step toward better pay.
